body:
## Problem Statement

Players can gather in a Room, choose Avatars, declare Ready, and see each other move, but starting the Room does not yet begin a playable Mafia game. There are no hidden Roles, Night actions, private Mafia discussion, Meetings, elimination votes, or victory conditions. A group needs a complete, basic game loop that it can play from Start to a faction victory without a moderator, while retaining the existing Room, Avatar, and Reconnect experience.

## Solution

Build a seated, ten-Player Mafia Game with three Mafia and seven Village members: five Villagers, one Doctor, and one Sheriff. Require every Player to be connected and Ready before the Host starts. Randomly assign Roles, privately reveal the appropriate information, and automatically alternate Night actions with public Meeting discussion and voting until a faction wins.

Use text chat for public Meetings and a private Night channel for living Mafia. Keep all Players in their existing circular Seat arrangement; change the overlays, countdowns, and available actions as phases advance. A Player previews an action locally and explicitly confirms it once; confirmed choices cannot be changed or withdrawn. Preserve identity, secret information, history, and action locks through the existing recovery flow. Show eliminated Players as spectators, retain departed Players in the Game Roster, and reveal all Roles when the Game ends.

## User Stories

1. As a Host, I want Start to require exactly ten connected, Ready Players, so that the fixed Role distribution begins with a complete group.
2. As a Player, I want to keep my selected Avatar, Player Colour, identity, and Seat when the Game starts, so that I can recognize everyone throughout the Game.
3. As a Player, I want Roles assigned randomly and independently of appearance and seating, so that cosmetic choices do not determine my side.
4. As a Player, I want a private reveal of my Role and Faction, so that I understand my objective without exposing my identity to opponents.
5. As a Mafia Player, I want to know the other Mafia identities, so that we can coordinate as a team.
6. As a Village Player, I want other Players' Roles to remain secret until an authorized reveal, so that deduction matters.
7. As a Player, I want a brief initial role-reveal period before the first Night, so that I can understand my assignment.
8. As a Player, I want the server to advance phases automatically, so that the Game does not need a moderator or an active Host.
9. As a Player, I want the current phase and countdown to be visible, so that I know when I can act and when time expires.
10. As a Player, I want timed phases to retain their full duration after submissions, so that I retain discussion time and cannot infer secret Role activity from early endings.
11. As a Player, I want to remain seated throughout this version, so that I can focus on discussion and decisions.
12. As a Villager, I want a darkened sleep screen during Night, so that the Game clearly explains why I have no Night action.
13. As a Mafia Player, I want a private text channel during Night, so that I can discuss targets without Village Players or other Rooms receiving our messages.
14. As a Mafia Player, I want to confirm a vote for one living Village Player, so that I can contribute to the Night attack.
15. As a Mafia Player, I want to see my living teammates' confirmed target votes, so that I understand our committed choices.
16. As a Mafia Player, I want an attack to require more than half of living Mafia to agree, so that a single minority vote cannot determine the target.
17. As a Player, I want no attack when Mafia fail to reach a strict majority, so that disagreement has a predictable outcome.
18. As a Player, I want Mafia to attack at most one Player each Night, so that the elimination rules remain clear.
19. As the Doctor, I want to protect one living Player each Night, so that I can prevent the Mafia attack from killing that Player.
20. As the Doctor, I want to be able to protect myself, so that I can choose personal survival over protecting another Player.
21. As the Doctor, I want the previous Night's protected Player to be unavailable on the immediately following Night, so that I cannot protect one Player indefinitely on consecutive Nights.
22. As the Doctor, I want an idle Night to break the consecutive-protection restriction, so that I may protect an earlier target again after a gap.
23. As the Doctor, I want my action and its success to remain private, so that protection does not expose my Role or automatically confirm a save.
24. As the Sheriff, I want to investigate one other living Player per Night, so that I can learn whether they belong to Mafia.
25. As the Sheriff, I want an investigation to report only Mafia or Not Mafia at Night end, so that it does not reveal another Village Player's exact Role.
26. As the Sheriff, I want to be allowed to investigate a previous target again on a later Night, so that the targeting rules remain consistent.
27. As the Sheriff, I want my previous investigation results restored on Reconnect, so that a connection loss does not erase information I earned.
28. As a Player, I want a Sheriff killed during the Night to receive no investigation result for that Night, so that Night resolution has a clear outcome.
29. As a Player, I want to preview a target before explicitly confirming a choice, so that an incidental click does not irreversibly submit an action.
30. As a Player, I want every confirmed action or ballot to stay locked for its phase, so that everyone follows the same commitment rule.
31. As a Player, I want private target previews to stay on my own client, so that unconfirmed choices cannot influence other Players.
32. As a Player, I want an unsubmitted Night action or Meeting ballot to have no effect, so that the Game can continue when someone does not act.
33. As a Player, I want the Night outcome to announce who died without revealing their Role, so that survivors retain the intended uncertainty.
34. As a Player, I want a no-death announcement to avoid distinguishing no attack from successful protection, so that it does not leak the Doctor's success.
35. As a Night victim, I want to see "You were killed by the mafias" without attacker identities, so that my death is explained without disclosing hidden Players.
36. As a living Player, I want public text discussion during the Meeting, so that I can share suspicions and defend myself.
37. As a living Player, I want public text chat to remain available during voting, so that discussion can continue while ballots are submitted.
38. As a living Player, I want to vote for any living Player, including myself, so that the agreed voting rules allow self-votes.
39. As a living Player, I want an explicit Skip ballot, so that I can commit to avoiding an elimination.
40. As a Player, I want Meeting ballots hidden until voting closes and then attributed to their voters, so that live tallies do not influence voting while final accountability remains visible.
41. As a Player, I want Meeting elimination to require more than half of all living Players, so that a mere plurality is insufficient.
42. As a Player, I want ties, insufficient support, Skips, and missing ballots to produce no elimination unless a target still has the required majority, so that voting outcomes are predictable.
43. As a Player, I want an elimination animation to reveal Mafia or Not Mafia, so that the group learns the voted-out Player's Faction without identifying Doctor versus Sheriff.
44. As an eliminated Player, I want to watch public Meetings while remaining in the Room, so that I can follow the rest of the Game.
45. As a living Player, I want eliminated Players unable to chat, act, or vote, so that they cannot influence the remaining Game through its controls.
46. As an eliminated Mafia Player, I want to retain messages I previously received but receive no later Mafia chat, so that elimination does not grant continuing private access.
47. As a Player, I want eliminated Avatars dimmed and marked Eliminated, so that I can distinguish spectators from living targets.
48. As a Player, I want departed Players' Seats left empty and marked Left without moving anyone else, so that spatial identification stays stable.
49. As a Player, I want public Meeting history and my authorized private chat restored on Reconnect, so that I can resume with the information I previously had.
50. As a Player, I want history confined to its Game and Room, so that another Room cannot access our conversations.
51. As a disconnected Player, I want the existing 120-second recovery reservation to preserve my Role, identity, and living status, so that temporary connection loss is not an immediate elimination.
52. As a Player, I want phase clocks to continue through Disconnects, so that an unavailable participant does not stall the Game.
53. As a Player, I want disconnected living Players to remain valid targets and count toward majorities and victory, so that Disconnect cannot be used to avoid participation rules.
54. As a recovering Player, I want to return to the current phase with my accepted action still locked, so that refreshing does not enable a second choice.
55. As a Player, I want Leave or recovery expiry to cause a living Player to Forfeit, so that permanently absent Players no longer count toward the Game outcome.
56. As a Player, I want a forfeiting actor's pending actions and ballots removed, so that departed Players cannot act later in the phase.
57. As a Player, I want a choice targeting a forfeited Player to become ineffective without unlocking a replacement, so that commitment remains consistent even when the target leaves.
58. As a Player, I want Forfeits reflected in living counts and victory immediately, so that the Game ends when a faction has already won.
59. As a Player, I want all original Players retained in voting history and the final roster, so that departures do not erase the explanation of the Game's result.
60. As a Village Player, I want Village to win when no Mafia remain alive, so that our objective has a clear completion condition.
61. As a Mafia Player, I want Mafia to win when living Mafia equal or outnumber living Village Players, so that parity ends the contest.
62. As a Player, I want all Roles revealed on the final result screen, so that I can understand how the Game unfolded.
63. As a Player, I want the final results to remain available while I stay in the Room, so that I have time to review them.
64. As a Player, I want another Game to require a new Room, so that a completed Game is not silently reset or reopened to newcomers.
65. As a Player, I want duplicate Display Names and Avatar choices to remain distinguishable through Player identity, so that actions affect the intended person.
66. As a Player, I want private information and action permissions enforced by the server, so that inspecting messages or bypassing disabled controls cannot reveal secrets or grant extra actions.

## Implementation Decisions

- Extend the existing Room lifecycle with a server-owned Game and phase progression. Keep the existing single-process, in-memory architecture and versioned WebSocket transport. A separate Game Roster records original participation independently of current Room Memberships, as established by ADR 0012.
- Update the Host Start gate from the existing testing behavior to exactly ten connected, Ready Players. Assign exactly three Mafia, five Villagers, one Doctor, and one Sheriff randomly at Start, independently of cosmetics and Seat order. Preserve accepted Avatar choices and existing identity. Repeated Start cannot reassign Roles.
- Extend the Room/Game state, message handling, client protocol decoding and builders, network inbox application, world state, reconnect flow, Avatar reconciliation, and scene/interface presentation. Introduce the Night action, Meeting ballot, private Role/result, phase/deadline, roster status, and chat interfaces needed for the Game. Keep the Java contract, TypeScript contract, and protocol documentation synchronized; exact wire names are implementation work, not prescribed by this spec.
- Separate public state from information authorized for a particular recipient. Own Role, Mafia team identities, Mafia Night votes and chat, Doctor choice, Sheriff choice/results, and hidden Meeting ballots must not be sent to unauthorized clients and merely concealed in the UI. Recovery must rebuild the recipient's authorized current view and history without leaking other Players' secrets. Final results deliberately reveal all Roles.
- Use Player ID to identify actors and targets; Display Names and Avatar Presets can repeat. Derive the actor and Room from the authorized connection. Validate Role, living status, target eligibility, current phase, deadline, and existing submission before accepting an action. Retired takeover sockets have no authority. Delayed requests must not become actions for a different Night or Meeting.
- Resolve Start, submissions, deadlines, Forfeits, recovery, and outbound event creation under the existing per-Room serialization. Do not write sockets while holding Room locks. Continue using bounded asynchronous outboxes; structural Game transitions and chat must not be treated as replaceable movement updates. Preserve the existing overflow/recovery behavior.
- Apply network events through the inbox at game-frame boundaries. Server phase progression is independent of client frame rendering, tab visibility, and Host presence. Client countdowns present server-owned timing rather than authorizing actions or outcomes.
- Preserve Seats throughout the Game and reject movement that would leave the static seated arrangement. Reuse the circular Meeting Area and seated Avatars. A phase change or Reconnect must not reseat or reorder everyone. Eliminated Avatars are dimmed and marked Eliminated; departed Players leave empty Seats marked Left. All original Players remain in the Game Roster for history and final results.
- Use an 8-second initial private Role reveal, then cycles of 90-second Night, 6-second Night outcome, 120-second discussion, 30-second voting, and 6-second voting result. Timed phases run their full duration even after all submissions; a victory still terminates the contest. The server runs the loop automatically, including when the Host is disconnected or eliminated. There are no pause, phase-skip, or restart controls.
- During Night, ordinary Villagers see a darkened sleep screen and countdown. Living Mafia, Doctor, and Sheriff receive only their appropriate private action controls. Each Night uses one shared deadline for all Night actions.
- Target selection first creates a local preview. An explicit Confirm vote, Confirm protection, or Confirm investigation action submits it. The first accepted submission is immutable for that phase, including a Meeting Skip. Do not permit change or withdrawal after acceptance. Restore accepted choices and locks on recovery; do not broadcast unconfirmed previews.
- Living Mafia may vote only for a living Village Player. Teammates can see confirmed Mafia votes. Attack only when more than half of living Mafia agree on one target: two of three, two of two, or one of one. Count disconnected living Mafia. No strict majority means no attack; at most one Player is attacked each Night.
- Doctor may protect one living Player, including themselves, but not the Player protected on the immediately preceding Night. An idle Night breaks the consecutive-target restriction. Protection blocks the attack only when the protected Player is the attack target. If Mafia kill the Doctor while another Player is protected, there is no second attack for that protection to block. Self-protection can save the Doctor. No submission means no protection, and the Doctor receives no success confirmation.
- Sheriff may investigate one other living Player each Night and may repeat a previous target on a later Night. Deliver only Mafia or Not Mafia at Night end. A Sheriff killed that Night receives no result. Retain previous private investigation results across recovery.
- Resolve the Night actions together before checking victory. Publicly name the victim without revealing their Role, or announce that nobody died without identifying whether protection or lack of an attack caused it. A successfully killed victim sees "You were killed by the mafias" with no attacker or Mafia voter identity.
- Public text chat is available to living Players during Meeting discussion and voting. Private Mafia text chat is available only to living Mafia during Night. Eliminated Players can watch public Meetings but cannot send chat, vote, act, or receive later Mafia chat. There is no ghost chat or private Mafia chat outside Night.
- Retain public Meeting history and each Player's previously authorized private chat for the current Game, restoring them on Reconnect. Eliminated Mafia retain earlier messages but receive no subsequent messages. Histories are scoped to their Game and Room and disappear when the Room is removed. Chat is text, not executable markup.
- Meeting ballots may target any living Player, including the voter, or explicitly Skip. Keep ballots hidden until the voting deadline, then disclose who voted for whom. Eliminate only when a target receives more than half of all living Players' votes; disconnected living Players still count in that denominator. Skips and missing ballots do not lower the threshold. Ties or insufficient votes mean no elimination.
- The Meeting result animation reveals Mafia or Not Mafia for the eliminated Player; it does not identify Doctor versus Sheriff. A Night death does not publicly reveal its victim's Role. Preserve the distinction between Elimination and Leave: eliminated Players may retain Room Membership and spectate.
- Disconnect preserves a living Player's status and membership for the existing 120-second recovery window. Clocks continue, accepted submissions remain, and missing submissions have no effect. Disconnected living Players remain eligible targets and count toward majorities and victory. Preserve same-tab recovery, credential-based takeover, retired-socket isolation, and transport health behavior.
- Leave or recovery expiry causes a living Player to Forfeit. Remove that actor's pending actions and ballots. Choices aimed at the forfeiting target become ineffective and remain locked, with no replacement allowed that phase. Compute phase-result majorities from the living roster at resolution. Leaving after elimination does not change living counts. Forfeit can decide victory; it does not abort the Game.
- Check victory after Night resolution, Meeting elimination, and Forfeit. If no living Mafia remain, Village wins. Otherwise, if living Mafia equal or exceed living Village Players, Mafia wins. Finish the Game and reveal all original Players' Roles. Final results remain until Players leave, subject to existing recovery and Room lifetime rules.
- Preserve the prohibition on fresh Join after Start and the final-membership removal rule in ADR 0009. A retained Game Roster is historical participation, not a Room Membership, recovery credential, or reason to keep an empty Room alive. A new Game requires a new Room; do not reset a started Room to Lobby.
- Update existing tests and documentation that assume Start accepts unready or incomplete groups, clears Seats, or opens free movement. Preserve the architectural requirements for versioned strict decoding, frame-boundary application, per-Room serialization, bounded delivery, Avatar publication, and resumable membership. The approved glossary and roster-retention ADR describe the intended domain model; implementation must bring runtime behavior into agreement.

## Testing Decisions

- Prefer externally observable behavior over internal method calls, object layouts, or duplicated implementation logic. A good test submits a real protocol request or simulates an actual connection/timing event and asserts messages, permissions, rendered behavior, or a Game outcome visible to the relevant Player.
- Use the existing WebSocket handler boundary as the main automated seam. The current handler tests already use recording WebSocket sessions, deterministic identifiers, controllable clocks, Room management, recovery, and competing operations. Extend that approach to ten Players and advance time without sleeping through full Nights. Exercise the real rule and recipient-visibility logic rather than replacing it with mocks.
- Use deterministic control of assignment when a scenario requires a specific Role, while separately verifying the assignment's exact distribution and independence from cosmetics. Do not rely on probabilistic tests to prove randomness or inspect internal role containers instead of the authorized outputs.
- Cover the Start gate for too few Players, Not Ready Players, disconnected reservations, non-Host requests, and repeated Start. Verify private role reveal, correct faction membership, Seat continuity, and rejection of movement during the seated Game.
- At the message boundary, exercise successful Mafia majorities, split votes, missing actions, Doctor self-protection, consecutive-target rejection, an idle-Night cooldown break, Sheriff repeat investigations, and the absence of a result for a Sheriff killed that Night. Assert the generic victim message and the indistinguishable public no-death announcement.
- Verify that local preview is not a submission, every accepted choice locks, Meeting self-votes and Skip work, a second submission cannot alter the first, and reconnect does not clear the lock. Test stale or late actions and submissions competing with phase expiry or Forfeit; outcomes must correspond to one consistent Room order.
- Test Meeting majorities against all living Players, including disconnected ones. Cover ties, abstentions, Skips, insufficient plurality, and changed living counts after Forfeit. Verify final ballot disclosure and faction-only elimination reveals.
- Assert private-data absence in each unauthorized recipient's complete payload stream, including snapshots, errors, recovery, and history. Exercise Village, living Mafia, eliminated Mafia, other eliminated Players, an unrelated Room, and retired sockets. Client-side concealment alone is not a passing privacy test.
- Exercise public versus Mafia chat permissions by phase and living status. Verify recovery of authorized history, retention of older Mafia messages after elimination, and the absence of later private messages for eliminated recipients. Confirm text is displayed as text.
- Cover Disconnect versus Forfeit, accepted choices during disconnection, recovery before expiry, expiry and intentional Leave, invalidated targets without replacement, roster retention after membership removal, and Host loss without a stalled Game. Test both victory conditions, Forfeit-triggered victory, final role disclosure, prohibition of fresh Join, and final Room removal.
- Extend existing frontend protocol, frame-boundary, reconnect, and seating tests only for client responsibilities. Prior art includes strict protocol decoding, ordered inbox application, fake-socket recovery with controlled time, and seated Avatar transitions. Verify Game events do not mutate the view before a frame boundary, recovery restores current private state and locks, and phase changes do not replay arrival or reorder Seats. Avoid duplicating the entire server rule matrix in frontend unit tests.
- Verify the complete experience with the backend running, a healthy health endpoint, the client served on the supported development port, and ten independent browser clients. Exercise Role reveal, Night controls, private/public chat, confirmation and locking, Meeting ballots, outcome animations, spectator state, recovery, and a completed Game. Inspect unauthorized clients for hidden-data leakage. This is the highest-level acceptance check and complements the existing automated seams; no new low-level test API is required by the spec.
- Run the complete affected backend suite, frontend suite including the authoring boundary tests, frontend typecheck, and production build. Use the backend packaging check if implementation changes startup or scheduling configuration. Report unit, protocol, and browser verification separately; passing one does not establish the others.

## Out of Scope

- Voice chat, ghost chat, and additional direct-message channels.
- Free movement, daytime exploration, tasks, map objectives, proximity mechanics, or combat animations involving moving Avatars.
- Variable Player counts, configurable Role distributions, additional Roles, or alternative victory rules.
- Revealing a Night attacker's identity, revealing exact Village Roles on Meeting elimination, or confirming Doctor saves.
- Editing or withdrawing accepted actions, replacement choices after a target Forfeit, and early phase completion after everyone submits.
- Host pause, phase-skip, restart, or moderator controls.
- Rematches within the same Room, resetting a started Room to Lobby, and fresh Join after Start.
- Persistent accounts, cross-device identity, databases, recovery across backend restarts, multi-server state coordination, or production deployment.
- Replacing the Avatar authoring/publication system or changing its boundary with the Player app.
- A new testing framework or comprehensive low-level unit-test surface solely for this feature; prefer the existing high-level boundaries.

## Further Notes

- This spec consolidates the agreed design interview. The later corrections are authoritative: the Doctor cannot protect the same Player on consecutive Nights; Night victims receive only the generic Mafia death message; Meeting self-votes are allowed; every confirmed action is immutable; and a forfeited target does not permit a replacement choice.
- The term Village includes five Villagers, the Doctor, and the Sheriff. Villager names the ordinary Role, not the entire Faction. Avatar, Display Name, Player ID, Role, and Faction remain distinct concepts.
- The current implementation has Lobby foundations and a free-movement phase, but none of the Mafia gameplay model. Existing unrestricted Start and standing-spawn expectations are deliberate testing behavior to replace, not constraints to preserve for this feature.
- ADR 0012 records why the Game Roster survives individual membership departure while ADR 0009 still removes a Room after its final membership ends. Other existing architectural decisions remain applicable.
- Documentation from the interview is preparatory work. No runtime Mafia implementation or verification is claimed by publication of this spec.
title: Build the basic ten-player Mafia game loop
